title: Cooling Tower Cycles of Concentration — Monitoring
equipment: Conductivity meter or chloride test kit
reagents: Chloride titration reagents (if using Cl- method)
steps: Collect a makeup water sample and a blowdown (or tower basin) water sample at the same time.
Measure conductivity (or chloride) on both samples using the same method.
Enter both values into the Cycles of Concentration calculator.
Compare the result to the target COC for the system; adjust blowdown rate if outside target range.

title: Boiler Blowdown — Procedure and Sampling
equipment: Sample cooler (if sampling from a hot line)
steps: Confirm blowdown valve and sample cooler are in service and cooled to a safe handling temperature.
Flush the sample line for at least 1-2 minutes before collecting a sample.
Collect the sample in a clean bottle, avoiding overflow/splash.
Test boiler water TDS/conductivity and other required parameters promptly.
Use the Boiler % Blowdown calculator with feedwater and max allowed boiler TDS to verify blowdown rate is adequate.
Log results and any valve adjustments made in the Logbook.
safetyNotes: Blowdown water and lines can be extremely hot — use proper PPE and allow cooling before direct sampling.

title: Silica Testing — Colorimetric Method
steps: Collect a representative boiler water (or feedwater) sample in a silica-free container.
Add molybdate reagent and allow color development per kit instructions.
Add acid reagent to eliminate phosphate interference.
Add reducing agent and wait the specified development time.
Read silica concentration on the colorimeter/spectrophotometer.
Compare the result against the maximum allowed silica for the operating pressure using the Silica Carryover Check calculator.
safetyNotes: Handle acid reagent with gloves and eye protection.

title: Phosphate Residual — Colorimetric Method
steps: Collect a boiler water sample and allow it to cool to room temperature.
Fill the sample cell to the fill line.
Add the phosphate reagent and mix per kit instructions.
Wait the specified reaction time, then read on the colorimeter.
Compare the reading to the target residual; use the Phosphate Residual Dosing calculator to adjust chemical feed if needed.

title: Sulfite Residual — Titration Method
reagents: Standard titrant (e.g. phenylarsine oxide or iodine, per kit)
steps: Collect a fresh boiler water sample and test immediately (sulfite oxidizes quickly on exposure to air).
Measure the sample volume specified by the kit into a flask.
Add indicator and titrate to the specified endpoint.
Calculate residual using the kit's conversion, or the Sulfite Residual Dosing calculator to determine required feed adjustment.

title: Feedwater and Condensate Sampling
steps: Sample from designated feedwater and condensate return taps after adequate line flushing.
Allow samples to cool to a safe handling/testing temperature before analysis.
Test for the parameters required by the water treatment program (e.g. hardness, pH, conductivity, dissolved oxygen as applicable).
Use the Condensate Return % calculator with measured condensate and feedwater flows to track return percentage.
Log results and flag any out-of-range readings for follow-up.
safetyNotes: Condensate lines may be hot/pressurized — use proper PPE.

title: Conductivity Measurement
steps: Calibrate the meter against a known standard solution; recalibrate if drift is out of tolerance.
Rinse the probe with distilled water, then with a small volume of the sample.
Immerse the probe in the sample and allow the reading to stabilize.
Record conductivity (µS/cm) and sample temperature.
Use the Boiler Water TDS from Conductivity calculator if an estimated TDS is needed.
